etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English in-to, from Old English intō, equivalent to in +‎ to. Cognate with Scots intae.

definitions.definition: To or towards the inside of.

quote.citation: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter I, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC, page 2:
quote.text: He used to drop into my chambers once in a while to smoke, and was first-rate company. When I gave a dinner there was generally a cover laid for him. I liked the man for his own sake, and even had he promised to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me.

quote.citation: 2011 November 3, Chris Bevan, “Rubin Kazan 1-0 Tottenham”, in BBC Sport:
quote.text: This time Cudicini was left helpless when Natcho stepped up to expertly curl the ball into the top corner.

definitions.definition: To or towards the region of.
Against, especially with force or violence.
Indicates transition into another form or substance.

quote.citation: 2002, Matt Cyr, Something to Teach Me: Journal of an American in the Mountains of Haiti, Educa Vision, Inc., →ISBN, page 25:
quote.text: His English is still in its beginning stages, like my Creole, but he was able to translate some Creole songs that he's written into English—not the best English, but English nonetheless.

definitions.definition: Indicates division or the creation of subgroups or sections.

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Peter Wilby, “Finland spreads word on schools”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 30:
quote.text: Imagine a country where children do nothing but play until they start compulsory schooling at age seven. Then, without exception, they attend comprehensives until the age of 16. Charging school fees is illegal, and so is sorting pupils into ability groups by streaming or setting.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter XIII, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: " […]  They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably." And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.

quote.citation: 2021 August 13, Gayle, Sara Davis, David Pittenger, “abcdefu”, in A Study of the Human Experience Volume One‎[1], performed by Gayle:
quote.text: I was into you, but I'm over it now / And I was trying to be nice / But nothing's getting through, so let me spell it out […]

definitions.definition: (mathematics) Expressing the operation of division, with the denominator given first. Usually with "goes".
(British, archaic, India, mathematics) Expressing the operation of multiplication.[1]
